story_chant.reason: No story or chant is given; the lesson is only model sentences and writing items.

listen_do_steps.reason: All steps are 'write a sentence' or 'complete' items; no point/tap/say/draw/show listen-and-do instructions.

child_tone.reason: Messages are fairly short with 'Good try!' and 'Thanks for trying again', but the tutor labels examples 'Wrong:' twice and talks about a 'spelling slip'.

age_fit.reason: Family topic suits a 6-year-old, but the lesson relies on written sentences and letter-by-letter spelling checks that are demanding for this age.

teacher_accept.reason: Target 'This is my' and 'He/She is' are practised correctly, but the 'check father letter by letter' hint for 'mather' is unhelpful and the lesson is all writing for a 6-year-old.

task_goal.reason: Learner writes one work comparison sentence (office) and the manager meeting-room role-play only appears in the last turn, unanswered; most of the lesson is isolated spelling items.

feedback_after_task.reason: After the learner writes the office sentence, feedback targets only the one error 'biger'.

task_repeat.reason: The tutor asks for the office sentence again with the fix and later sets a new work task, but the learner never uses the fix within the work task (only in 'thinner' and a sentence about a brother).

age_fit.reason: Respectful adult tone and work-based examples (meetings, office, desk, meeting rooms).

teacher_accept.reason: Doubling rule is taught correctly, but the lesson is mostly spelling drills with little 'more ... than' or work communication, and the 'more hot' contrast does not match the learner's error.

short_sentences.reason: Only one tutor sentence is over 12 words ('Write one sentence about a person you know using -s or -es on the verb after he, she and it').

one_instruction.reason: Two messages ask for several things: turn 4 (look at the last letters, fix the verb, write the whole sentence again) and turn 6 (compare, look at the letters, decide the ending, write again).

praise_effort.reason: Praise is only 'correct', 'Good work' and 'that idea is right'; trying or effort is never praised.

game_story.reason: No game, challenge or story frame.

ppp_order.reason: The form is shown with examples, then controlled items (sleeps, plays), then the child writes their own sentence about their mother.

age_fit.reason: Short, clear messages with everyday topics (school, family, pets) suit a 12-year-old.

teacher_accept.reason: Teaching is correct, but the presentation gives only -s although the objective includes -es, so the -es errors repeat and the 'longer ending' hint is vague.

short_sentences.reason: Only one tutor sentence is over 12 words ('Now write one sentence about a person you know using the object correctly').

one_instruction.reason: Turn 2 asks the child to check the word, look letter by letter and write again; turn 6 asks the child to think about the board and then write a sentence.

praise_effort.reason: 'Good try!' twice and 'Good work on your own'.

game_story.reason: No game, challenge or story frame.

ppp_order.reason: 'This is a desk' model, then guided items (bag, book), then the child's own sentence ('My sister has a pencil').

age_fit.reason: Short, warm messages about classroom objects suit a 9-year-old.

teacher_accept.reason: Correct but thin: few objects are taught, and the 'sentence about a person using the object' step is awkward for a vocabulary lesson.

short_sentences.reason: Five or more tutor sentences are over 12 words, e.g. 'The answer here is "bigger": "big" ends in one vowel...', 'Tell me in your own words: what were you thinking...', and 'Then look at what happened to the last letter of "hot"...'.

one_instruction.reason: One message asks for several things (turn 5: look at thin, then look at hotter, then write again).

praise_effort.reason: Only one praise of the child's thinking ('Your rule about doubling the consonant is right'); the rest is 'correct'/'close'.

game_story.reason: No game, challenge or story frame.

ppp_order.reason: The form is shown with an example, then controlled items follow, but the lesson is cut before the child writes their own sentence.

age_fit.reason: The animal and Cairo topics suit a 10-year-old, but many sentences are long and use metalinguistic language ('one vowel and one consonant', 'what were you thinking').

teacher_accept.reason: The comparative and doubling rule are taught correctly, but the explanations are long for a 10-year-old and the Right/Wrong pairs (e.g. 'more red' marked wrong) do not address the child's actual error.
